# AGENTS.md — opencode-cron

This repo IS the opencode-cron plugin (scheduled tasks for opencode, ChatGPT-style).
Dev commands: `bun install && bun test && bun run typecheck && bun run build`.

## Dogfooding: this repo runs its own cron

- Jobs live in `.opencode/cron/jobs.json` (gitignored), memory in `.opencode/cron/memory/`.
- A launchd ticker (`ai.opencode.cron`, 60s) checks due jobs and admits tick prompts
  over HTTP into the desktop app's session server (`OPENCODE_PROMPT_HTTP` transport).

### Plugin installation (global)

opencode loads the plugin **globally** from the config dir, not from this repo:

```
~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-cron/index.ts   # re-exports <repo>/src/index.ts
```

`~/.config/opencode/plugins/` is the global plugin directory in opencode V2 (the
counterpart of a project's `.opencode/plugins/`) and every sub-directory with an
`index.ts` is loaded automatically. That is also what the desktop app lists under
Settings → Plugins, and what `/api/plugin` reports as
`{"type":"local","path":".../plugins/opencode-cron/index.ts"}`.

Do **not** add a second copy of the plugin inside the repo (`.opencode/plugin/` or
`.opencode/plugins/`): two sources with the same plugin `id` make the second one
fail with `Duplicate plugin ID: opencode-cron`. The wrapper above keeps the repo
as the single source of truth.

## Desktop credentials rotation (important)

The desktop app rotates its sidecar credentials on every restart. The ticker reads
them from `~/.config/opencode-cron/credentials` (0600), falling back to the live
password in `~/.config/opencode/service.json` (opencode 2.1 desktop stores it
there and no longer injects `OPENCODE_SERVER_*` into agent turns). After an app
restart ticks fail with HTTP 401 until the credentials are refreshed. So: if the
user mentions the cron stopped working, or jobs show `consecutiveFailures` climbing
with 401 errors, run:

```bash
node ./dist/bin/run.js refresh-creds
```

(and reset `consecutiveFailures` to 0 / re-enable the job if it auto-paused).
The `/cron-refresh` slash command wraps the same flow.

Note: the sidecar exposes the API at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/...` (the
port is logged by the desktop app as `v2 CLI background service ready { url: ... }`).
`POST /api/session/:id/prompt` requires the text at the root of the payload.

It helps AI engineers discover true agent scheduling. --- ## 🚀 Why opencode-cron? Traditional cron is **blind**: it runs an isolated shell script, forgets previous executions, loses conversational context, and can burn hundreds of dollars in looping API tokens. **opencode-cron is an intelligent AI Agent Scheduler:** * 🔄 **Same Conversation, Every Tick:** It re-prompts the **same `sessionID`** with full conversation history, not a detached CLI call. * 🧠 **Persistent Markdown Memory:** Survives context compaction, restarts, and reboots. Tracks `seenHashes` to prevent repetitive notifications. * 🖥️ **Mission Control Web GUI:** Sleek dark-mode dashboard at `http://localhost:4488` with live SQLite chat streaming, active job monitors, and instant controls. * 🪟 **Cross-Platform Desktop App & System Tray:** Native installable packages for **macOS (.dmg)**, **Windows (.exe)**, and **Linux (.AppImage, .deb)** with a live system tray icon showing real-time OpenCode connection and active cron status. * ⚡ **1-Click "Imposta Cron" Binding:** Bind an automated recurring schedule directly to any conversation session with visual schedule previews. * 📊 **Execution Timeline & Diagnostics (`/runs`):** Real-time visibility into every tick: duration, status, exit codes, trigger source, and error logs. * ⚡ **Smart Adaptive Schedule & Burst Mode:** Dynamically accelerates into high-frequency cadence (e.g. 1m) upon activity/discoveries and backs off to idle (e.g. 30m) when quiet, conserving LLM tokens while reacting instantly. Includes 1-click 15m Burst trigger in the GUI and `cron_burst` Code Mode tool. * 🔗 **Multi-Job Pipeline & DAG Workflows:** Chain tasks with `onSuccess` / `onFailure` triggers, memory propagation, and cycle prevention. * 📡 **Inbound Webhooks & HTTP Trigger Receiver:** External event triggers with HMAC SHA-256 signatures (GitHub, GitLab, CI/CD). * ⚡ **Priority Concurrency & Worker Pool:** Parallel bounded worker slots (1 to 10) with priority queue sorting (`high`, `normal`, `low`). * 🛡️ **Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) & Failure Circuit Breaker:** Automatic quarantine after failures with canary probe recovery. * 🏷️ **Job Tags & Multi-Criteria Live Filtering:** Instant search, dynamic categories, tag pills, and matching counters. * 📈 **Real-Time Execution Metrics & Prometheus Exporter:** Latency KPIs (`avg`, `min`, `max`, `p95`) and scraping at `/api/metrics/prometheus`. * 🔔 **Multi-Channel Alerting:** Instant notifications via Slack, Discord, or custom HTTP webhooks with anti-spam cooldowns. * 📋 **Job Template & Blueprint Engine:** 6 built-in blueprints with 1-click apply and custom ID validation. * 💾 **Point-in-Time Snapshot & Backup/Restore Engine:** Instant backup bundles with SHA-256 verification and auto-pruning. * ⏱️ **Execution Timeout Watchdog:** Terminate hung ticks (minimum 5,000ms floor) across headless daemons and in-process plugins. * 🧹 **Run History Retention Policy:** Auto-prune by age, run count, or total history size. * 🌐 **Timezone-Aware Scheduling & Cron Aliases:** Full IANA timezone support and macros (`@hourly`, `@daily`, `@weekly`, etc.). * 🚦 **Pre-Flight Guards & Condition Checks:** Verify HTTP status or shell commands before spending tokens on ticks. * 🔐 **Secret & Credential Redaction Engine:** Sanitize AI keys, Bearer tokens, private keys, and webhook secrets from logs and history. * 🛡️ **Autonomous Background Daemon:** Keeps running overnight with your TUI or terminal closed via native `launchd`, `systemd`, or `schtasks`. --- ## ⚡ Plain Cron vs. opencode-cron | Feature | Plain Cron / Bash Loops | opencode-cron | |---|---|---| | **Session Awareness** | ❌ Spawns blind one-off shells | ✅ **Re-prompts same session ID** with full context | | **Context Compact Safe** | ❌ Wiped out on conversation compact | ✅ **Compaction hook re-injects memory file** | | **Deduplication** | ❌ Repeats same alerts every tick | ✅ **`seenHashes` dedup prevents repeat alerts** | | **Loop / Token Protection** | ❌ Can loop infinitely, burning tokens | ✅ **60s min, 5-fail circuit breaker, `maxRuns`, timeout guard** | | **User Interface** | ❌ Terminal only / crontab file | ✅ **Web GUI Mission Control (`localhost:4488`) + Desktop Tray** | | **Observability** | ❌ Grepping obscure syslog files | ✅ **Dedicated `/runs` Timeline + Prometheus Exporter** | | **Pipelines & DAG** | ❌ Fragile custom shell piping | ✅ **Native `onSuccess` / `onFailure` DAG with cycle checks** | | **External Triggers** | ❌ Custom listening scripts required | ✅ **Authenticated Webhooks (`/api/webhook/:id`)** | | **Multi-Language** | ❌ English only / none | ✅ **10 languages with interactive onboarding tour** | --- ## Normal prompt state is compressed or discarded. **opencode-cron hooks into `ctx.session.hook("compaction")`** to re-inject `.opencode/cron/memory/.md` directly into the compaction summary. Your agent retains 100% of its learned state, discovered URLs, and deduplication hashes. --- ## 🛡️ Production Guardrails & Reliability Designed for production workstations and autonomous background operations: * **Minimum 60s Interval:** Prevents runaway recursive loops and excessive API charges. * **Atomic Concurrency Locks:** `.lock` files prevent duplicate ticks if a previous execution is still running (`skipIfRunning: true`). * **Circuit Breaker Auto-Pause:** If an agent fails 5 consecutive times, the job auto-quarantines into the Dead Letter Queue. * **Execution Timeout Watchdog:** Terminate hung ticks (minimum 5,000ms floor) across daemons and plugins. * **Pre-Flight Guards:** Skip ticks when health checks fail, preventing wasted LLM credits. * **Secret Redaction:** Strip sensitive keys and tokens from logs, run history, and notifications. * **Self-Check Before Action:** Every tick prompt enforces a 3-question self-audit before making edits or API calls. --- ## 🔒 Security & Desktop Credentials Rotation The OpenCode desktop app rotates internal sidecar credentials on every restart. opencode-cron handles this automatically: 1. # opencode-cron - Launch Site

A single-page marketing / launch site for **opencode-cron**, built to be hosted
for free on **GitHub Pages**. No build step, no framework - just HTML, CSS,
vanilla JS and [Three.js](https://threejs.org) (via CDN import map).

## What's inside

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | The whole landing page (semantic, SEO + GEO optimized) |
| `assets/css/styles.css` | Design system (dark, glassy - matches the product GUI) |
| `assets/js/i18n.js` | 10-language dictionary (en, it, es, fr, de, pt, zh, ja, ru, ar-RTL) + engine |
| `assets/js/config.js` | **Single source of truth** for contact email, links, identity |
| `assets/js/hero3d.js` | Three.js hero animation (glowing agent core + orbiting task nodes) |
| `assets/js/app.js` | Nav, language picker, scroll reveal, FAQ, counters, contact form |
| `assets/img/` | favicon + social preview (OG image) |
| `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`, `ai.txt` | SEO + GEO / AI-crawler files |
| `manifest.webmanifest` | PWA manifest |
| `404.html` | Themed not-found page |
| `.nojekyll` | Tells GitHub Pages to serve files as-is (no Jekyll processing) |

## Deploy to GitHub Pages

1. Push this `site/` folder to the `main` branch.
2. In the repo: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**.
3. The workflow `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes `site/` automatically.
4. The site will be live at `https://culturedigitali.github.io/opencode-cron/`.

> Because this is a **project** Pages site, all internal links are rooted at
> `/opencode-cron/`. Keep that prefix when adding new assets.

## Configure your contact email

Open `assets/js/config.js` and set:

```js
contactEmail: "you@yourdomain.com"   // used by the contact form + footer
```

By default the contact form opens the visitor's mail client (`mailto:`).
To use a form backend instead (Formspree, Basin, Netlify…), set `formEndpoint`
in the same file - the form will then POST there.

## Local preview

Any static server works, e.g.:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory site
# then open http://localhost:8080/
```

Note: opening `index.html` via `file://` won't load the ES-module Three.js hero
(module CORS). Use a local server as above.

# AI agent cron jobs with opencode

Recurring agent work fits jobs, not one-shots: watchers, monitors, digests, triage.

| Case | Schedule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| AI news + X watcher | `every: 5m` | new items only, `STATS.json` updated |
| Competitor / price monitor | `every: 15m` | diff alert in same session |
| CI flaky re-check | `every: 10m` | re-runs, auto-pause after 5 fails |
| Changelog digest | `every: 1h` | daily markdown, compact-safe |
| Lead triage | `cron: */30 * * * *` | top 10 new, `seenHashes` tracked |

Pattern per tick: read memory (`cron_memory_read`) → self-check (what do I know / what's missing / must I re-read files?) → act → `cron_memory_save`. Zero-news ticks only update `lastRun`.

# ChatGPT scheduled tasks in opencode - parity notes

ChatGPT Scheduled Tasks = recurring prompt, executed by the model, with memory of past runs.

opencode-cron = same concept, local and session-bound:

| ChatGPT | opencode-cron |
|---|---|
| recurring prompt | `followupPrompt` on `every` / `cron` |
| same thread continues | same `sessionID` re-prompted |
| remembers past runs | `memory/<id>.md` + `seenHashes`, survives compact |
| runs while away | OS runner (launchd/systemd/schtasks) with TUI closed |

Difference: everything is a file in your project (`.opencode/cron/`), inspectable and versionable. Trade-off: the host must run the 60s ticker for TUI-closed execution.

# opencode-cron vs plain cron

Use plain cron / systemd timers for pure shell work (backups, `apt update`, log rotation). Use opencode-cron when the task needs judgment every run.

| | plain cron | opencode-cron |
|---|---|---|
| Executor | shell | same opencode `sessionID` |
| Context | none | frozen prompt + persistent memory + history |
| Compact | n/a (no context) | hook re-injects memory |
| Dedup | manual | `seenHashes` + locks |
| Cost control | free | 60s min, jitter, `maxRuns`, 5-fail pause |

Don't use opencode-cron for sub-60s polling or one-shots - `cron_run_now` covers the one-shot case.

# opencode scheduled tasks - how it works

`cron_add` stores a job in `.opencode/cron/jobs.json` plus a memory file `memory/<id>.md`.

## TUI open

The in-process `CronScheduler` arms one timer per enabled job (10% jitter). On fire, `executeTick`:

1. skips if disabled / `maxRuns` reached / session busy (`skipIfRunning`)
2. reads `memory/<id>.md` and builds the tick prompt: frozen system prompt + memory + mandatory 3-question self-check + followup
3. calls `ctx.session.prompt({ sessionID, text })` - the same chat continues
4. bumps `runCount`, recomputes `nextRunAt` (cron expression via `cron-parser` or interval), writes `runs/<id>.log`

## TUI closed

The OS adapter (`os-install`) installs a 60s ticker: launchd plist on macOS, systemd timer (crontab fallback) on Linux, schtasks on Windows. Each wake runs `opencode-cron-run check --dir <proj>`, which executes due jobs via `opencode run --session <id>` under an atomic lock file.

## Compact safety

The `compaction` session hook (`ctx.session.hook("compaction")`) injects `memory/<id>.md` into the compaction summary. Memory is the source of truth - chat history may compact, the file does not.

Guards: 60s minimum interval, 20 jobs max per project, 8k prompt caps, 32k memory cap with 200-hash dedup window, no catch-up by default, 5 consecutive failures auto-pause.

# opencode session cron - background tasks with launchd / systemd

The OS ticker runs every 60s and executes due jobs. Install once per project:

```bash

```

| OS | What gets installed |
|---|---|

| Linux | systemd user service + timer (60s), crontab fallback line |
| Windows | `schtasks` minute task |

Verify:

```bash

npx @culturedigitali/opencode-cron run <jobId> --dir /path/to/project
```

Labels are validated (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`), paths XML/shell-escaped, lock files make overlapping wakes safe (stale steal after 10 min).

# opencode persistent memory cron - the anti-compact design

Each job owns `memory/<id>.md` plus `<id>.state.json` (`seenHashes`, counts, failures).

- Created by `cron_add` from the frozen system prompt; updated only via `cron_memory_save` at end of tick.
- Injected into every tick prompt as source of truth, and into the compaction summary via the `compaction` session hook (`ctx.session.hook("compaction")`).
- Caps: 32k chars markdown, last 200 hashes kept, `.bak` backup on each save.
- `removeJob` deletes md + state + backup + run log + lock - no orphans.

Rule for the model: if memory says a URL was seen, it was seen. Never re-save it. Never paste secrets into memory (see `SECURITY.md`).

# opencode background tasks - troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Job never fires, TUI closed | run `os-install` for this project; check the ticker exists (launchctl / systemctl / schtasks) |
| Job paused by itself | 5 consecutive failures auto-pause - inspect `runs/<id>.log`, fix, `cron_resume` |
| Tick skipped | session busy (`skipIfRunning`) or lock held by overlapping run - wait one interval |
| Duplicates | check `seenHashes` in memory state; zero-news ticks must still call `cron_memory_save` |
| `jobs.json` corrupted | restore from backup / git; loader fails open to `[]` by design - keep the file in version control |

Logs: `~/.opencode-cron.log` (cron fallback), `~/Library/Logs/opencode-cron.log` (macOS). Inspect jobs with `cron_list` / `cron_get`.

# opencode-cron

> ChatGPT Scheduled Tasks for opencode - session-bound cron + persistent markdown memory for AI agents, by Culture Digitali Srl.

opencode-cron is an open-source (MIT) plugin for opencode that brings ChatGPT-style Scheduled Tasks to AI coding agents. Unlike plain cron, it re-prompts the same AI session on every scheduled tick with persistent memory, so the agent keeps full context, deduplicates alerts, and avoids burning tokens.

# Global cron dashboard

## Intent and approval

The user needs one page to find and manage cron jobs created in different conversations and projects. They approved a global default dashboard with project filtering, activation, pause, editing, schedule, next execution, last outcome and errors. Existing jobs must not be moved, copied, recreated or executed as part of discovery or testing.

This is an architectural extension: the current GUI and API are bound to a single directory at server startup.

## Approach

Use one global landing page and retain the existing project dashboard behind a project-scoped URL. Alternatives are separate servers/tabs per project (fragmented management) or moving every job into a global store (breaks ownership, memory and scheduling). Neither meets the intent safely.

### Project discovery

- A small registry in the user's opencode-cron configuration directory records canonical project directories, not jobs or credentials.
- Plugin operations register their project so future jobs become discoverable outside conventional workspace folders.
- Discover existing projects from the current project, the registry, available session database directories, and bounded scanning of configured workspace roots (default Desktop). Skip dependency directories, VCS internals and symlinks. Never recursively scan the whole home directory or filesystem.
- Tests inject temporary registry and workspace roots; they never register fixtures in the real user configuration.
- Canonical paths are deduplicated; stable opaque project IDs are derived from canonical paths. A project path supplied by a browser is never accepted as a filesystem target.
- Refresh updates the project catalog; discovery limits or unreadable projects produce visible warnings rather than a false 'all clear'.

### HTTP boundaries

- `/` becomes the global dashboard. Existing `/api/jobs`, `/api/status`, `/runs` and `/instructions` remain compatible with the startup project.
- `GET /api/projects` returns discovered projects and discovery warnings.
- `GET /api/global/jobs` returns project-qualified job summaries and warnings. Summaries exclude webhook tokens, secrets and prompts.
- `/p/:projectId/` and `/p/:projectId/api/...` dispatch to the existing project GUI and handlers without opening extra listening ports. Project-page navigation and fetches remain scoped.
- A job's management identity is `(projectId, jobId)`, never `jobId` alone. Unknown IDs, traversal and cross-site mutations are rejected before dispatch.
- Existing mutation semantics and validation are reused. A project context has its own concurrency manager; there is no process-wide mutable 'selected directory'.

### Global UI

- Match the existing light canvas/navy visual system with accessible native controls and responsive layout, without adding dependencies.
- Default to all projects and all states; show counts and project groups. Provide project, state and text filters. Clearing filters resets all of them.
- Each job shows title, project/path, conversation ID (title where available), schedule/timezone, enabled/paused/completed/quarantined state, next and last execution, run count, last known outcome and consecutive failures.
- 'Abilitato' means configured to run, not verified scheduler health. Missing outcome evidence is shown as unknown, not success.
- Explicit Attiva/Pausa commands use the project-qualified API. Editing supports title, prompts, schedule/timezone, target conversation and max executions; preserve unrelated job fields.
- Editing loads details only from the chosen project's endpoint, not the public summary. Show validation errors in the dialog and preserve user input. Prevent repeated submissions; restore focus on close; support Escape and keyboard navigation.
- 'Apri progetto' exposes the existing full-featured dashboard, memory and history. Include a prominent way back to all projects.
- Loading, empty, filtered-empty, network failure and partial-discovery states are distinct. Periodic refresh must not overwrite an open edit form.

## Adjacent defect in scope

The existing job renderer references removed `activeCount` and `totalRuns` variables inside its card map. Remove those stale increments (the aggregate KPI pass already computes both) and add a runtime regression test so project job cards are actually usable.

## Safety and scope

- No new runtime dependencies; keep Node/Bun portability and loopback-only binding.
- Do not change schedule execution, enable/disable production jobs, trigger agent prompts, rotate credentials, publish a release or push Git changes as part of the feature.
- Do not promise scheduler health from stored enabled flags. Existing ticker coverage is independent of this management view.
- Read-only browser checks on real projects; all mutation checks use isolated fixture projects with duplicate job IDs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The live landing page lists the four known enabled jobs across four projects and also exposes paused jobs.
2. Search and project/state filters work; project-qualified IDs prevent cross-project edits when job IDs coincide.
3. Edit and pause/resume persist after reload in isolated fixtures; invalid input leaves files untouched.
4. Project dashboards still render cards and all their API requests/navigation remain project-scoped.
5. Unknown project IDs, traversal and foreign-origin writes are rejected. A corrupt/inaccessible project does not hide healthy projects or appear empty without warning.
6. Discovery works with spaces/non-ASCII paths, deduplicates aliases, avoids symlink loops and observes scan limits.
7. Unit/integration tests, full suite, typecheck and build pass; verify desktop and mobile UI in a real browser and inspect console errors.

## Delivery

Implement in verifiable slices: catalog/discovery; scoped HTTP routing; global UI and existing renderer regression; browser verification and documentation. No version bump or release tag in this work.
